{
  "claims": [
    {
      "cause": "Changes in monetary policy",
      "effect": "Inflation",
      "linking_explanation": "Monetary policy changes take 18 to 24 months to feed through to inflation, with the effect accumulating over that timeframe.",
      "document_reference": "Page 1, Introduction",
      "quantifications": "18 to 24 months",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Raising Bank Rate by 390 basis points",
      "effect": "Effect on the real economy and inflation",
      "linking_explanation": "The expectation is that raising the Bank Rate should have a noticeable effect on the real economy and inflation, but the long and variable lags and the sequence of shocks may have influenced the transmission.",
      "document_reference": "Page 2, Introduction",
      "quantifications": "390 basis points",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "Perhaps",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Sequence of shocks and embedding of inflation risks",
      "effect": "Change in expectations formation",
      "linking_explanation": "The sequence of shocks and embedding of inflation risks may lead to a troubling change in expectations formation via an increase in the share of backward-looking participants in the real economy.",
      "document_reference": "Page 2, Introduction",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Change in policy rate",
      "effect": "Behaviour of households and firms, and ultimately output and prices",
      "linking_explanation": "The change in policy rate affects financial markets, which then influences the behaviour of households and firms based on their expectations, subsequently affecting output and prices.",
      "document_reference": "Page 3, What is the transmission mechanism?",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Factors outside of the central bank's control and interactions among channels",
      "effect": "Amplification or dampening of the pass-through of policy choices",
      "linking_explanation": "These factors and interactions can either amplify or dampen the effectiveness of monetary policy transmission.",
      "document_reference": "Page 4, Transmission mechanism of monetary policy",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "claims": [
    {
      "cause": "Tightening in financial conditions",
      "effect": "Households cut back on consumption",
      "linking_explanation": "As the cost of borrowing rises, and the opportunity cost of spending increases as saving rates rise.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 2, Page 6",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Tightening in financial conditions",
      "effect": "Firms reduce investment",
      "linking_explanation": "In response to rising borrowing costs, and in anticipation of worsening demand conditions.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 2, Page 6",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Expectations about the future",
      "effect": "Influence the present",
      "linking_explanation": "Expectations can affect wages and prices directly, possibly before demand and supply conditions in goods and labour markets have changed.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 2, Page 6",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Shocks outside of the control of a central bank",
      "effect": "Influence the key channels of the transmission mechanism",
      "linking_explanation": "These include changes in fiscal policy, trade linkages in the global economy, commodity prices, and risk preferences.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 2, Page 6",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Use of forward guidance and quantitative easing (QE)",

      "document_reference": "Batch 2, Page 7",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "claims": [
    {
      "cause": "Tightening from a loose monetary stance",
      "effect": "Less effect on inflation",
      "linking_explanation": "Research finds that the extent to which monetary policy affects inflation depends on thresholds, with tightening from a loose stance having less of an effect on inflation than tightening from a tight stance.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 3, paragraph 1",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Falling policy rates and QE",
      "effect": "Widening of mortgage spreads",
      "linking_explanation": "Spreads widened as reference rates fell in response to falling policy rates and QE, but mortgage rates fell only very slowly over the next decade, indicating a lagged pass-through.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 3, paragraph 2",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Changes in reference rates",
      "effect": "Lagged pass-through to mortgage rates",
      "linking_explanation": "There is evidence of lagged pass-through from changes in policy rates to the rates households face on their mortgages, with mortgage rates tracking reference rates closely initially but with a lag.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 3, paragraph 3",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Changes in risk-free rates",
      "effect": "State-dependent pass-through to mortgage rates",
      "linking_explanation": "Pass-through from changes in risk-free rates to mortgage rates is highly state-dependent, suggesting more rapid transmission as interest rates rise and slower transmission as interest rates fall.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 3, paragraph 4",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "MPC's tightening in monetary policy",
      "effect": "Considerable downward effect on equity prices",
      "linking_explanation": "The MPC's tightening in monetary policy has had a considerable downward effect on equity prices over the last twelve months, as shown through a decomposition of moves in equity prices using a Dividend Discount Model.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 3, paragraph 5",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "claims": [
    {
      "cause": "Higher interest rates",
      "effect": "Weigh on equity prices",
      "linking_explanation": "Higher interest rates lead to future earnings and cash flows being discounted using a higher discount factor.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 4, paragraph 1",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Higher interest rates",
      "effect": "Signal a worsening economic outlook to financial markets",
      "linking_explanation": "Higher interest rates are perceived as a signal of a worsening economic outlook, which should dampen expected shareholder payouts and potentially increase risk premia.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 4, paragraph 1",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "MPC's monetary policy tightening",
      "effect": "Offset by a falling equity risk premium",
      "linking_explanation": "The positive contribution of a falling equity risk premium implies that equities have performed better than expected given interest rates and growth expectations.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 4, paragraph 3",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Rise in UK interest rates",
      "effect": "Sterling should appreciate relative to other currencies",
      "linking_explanation": "All other things being equal, a rise in UK interest rates should cause Sterling to appreciate relative to other currencies.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 4, paragraph 5",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "US policy and macroeconomic factors",
      "effect": "Outweighed the MPC's tightening, leading to Sterling depreciation",
      "linking_explanation": "The Federal Reserve's quicker pace of tightening and a better macroeconomic outlook in the US have outweighed the MPC's tightening, contributing to Sterling's depreciation.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 4, paragraph 6",
      "quantifications": "Sterling has depreciated by 10% versus the Dollar",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "Up until the end of 2022"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Persistent UK-specific risk premium",
      "effect": "Weighing on Sterling",
      "linking_explanation": "A persistent UK-specific risk premium captures the reduced appetite for Sterling assets more broadly, unrelated to direct pricing of monetary policy and future macroeconomic conditions.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 4, paragraph 7",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "claims": [
    {
      "cause": "Monetary policy changing the interest rate",
      "effect": "Influencing spending, investment, and saving behavior, including expectations, wage, and price setting",
      "linking_explanation": "By changing the interest rate, monetary policy affects borrowing costs in the economy, which in turn influences economic behaviors such as spending, investment, and saving, as well as expectations and wage and price setting.",
      "document_reference": "Page 12-13",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Markets looking forward to the expected peak in policy rates",
      "effect": "Financial conditions beginning to loosen",
      "linking_explanation": "The anticipation of a peak in policy rates leads markets to adjust, resulting in looser financial conditions than might otherwise be expected.",
      "document_reference": "Page 12",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Depreciation of Sterling and a falling equity risk premium",
      "effect": "Looser financial conditions",
      "linking_explanation": "The depreciation of Sterling and a falling equity risk premium, which have global factors embedded in them, contribute to looser financial conditions.",
      "document_reference": "Page 12",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Tightening monetary policy",
      "effect": "Potential increase in inflation in the short run",
      "linking_explanation": "Empirical models have shown that tightening monetary policy can result in an increase in inflation in the short run due to endogenous policy responses to forecasts of future inflation.",
      "document_reference": "Page 13",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "at least in the short run"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "claims": [
    {
      "cause": "1 percentage point monetary policy shock",
      "effect": "Persistent effect on the 1-year nominal interest rate",
      "linking_explanation": "The monetary policy shock affects the interest rate, lasting for around twelve months after the shock hits.",
      "document_reference": "Page 14, top left panel",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "lasting for around twelve months"
    },
    {
      "cause": "1 percentage point monetary policy shock",
      "effect": "Appreciation of the Sterling exchange rate index",
      "linking_explanation": "The shock appreciates the exchange rate with a peak effect at two to three months, consistent with the effect on the 1-year nominal interest rate, explained by the theory of interest rate differentials.",
      "document_reference": "Page 14, top right-hand panel",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "peak effect at two to three months"
    },
    {
      "cause": "1 percentage point monetary policy shock",
      "effect": "Delayed response on the level of real GDP",
      "linking_explanation": "Real GDP barely moves on impact and slowly falls with a statistically significant peak response of -1.25% after around two years, consistent with monetary policy lags and New Keynesian theory.",
      "document_reference": "Page 14",
      "quantifications": "statistically significant peak response of -1.25%",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "after around two years"
    },
    {
      "cause": "1 percentage point monetary policy shock",
      "effect": "Instantaneous negative effect on the level of CPI",
      "linking_explanation": "The fast pass-through of the monetary tightening likely relies on the exchange rate appreciating on impact.",
      "document_reference": "Page 14, bottom right panel",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "instantaneous"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Announced changes in the monetary policy rate",
      "effect": "Firms revise their price expectations, with rate hikes inducing a decrease in price expectations and uncertainty",
      "linking_explanation": "An event study shows evidence for a direct expectations channel of monetary policy affecting price setting within the period of the shock.",
      "document_reference": "Page 15",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "within the period of the shock"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "claims": [
    {
      "cause": "Higher degree of backward-looking inflation expectations",
      "effect": "More inflation persistence",
      "linking_explanation": "Backward-looking expectations cause individuals to base their future expectations on past inflation, leading to sustained inflation levels even if the underlying shock is the same.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 7",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Backward-looking inflation expectations",
      "effect": "Reduced effectiveness of monetary policy to control inflation",
      "linking_explanation": "When expectations are backward-looking, they become detached from current demand and supply conditions, making monetary policy less effective in controlling inflation.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 7",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Cost-push shock",
      "effect": "Exogenous increase in prices",
      "linking_explanation": "A cost-push shock increases prices beyond what domestic demand conditions would imply, representing external factors like global goods or energy price shocks.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 7",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Introduction of backward-looking inflation expectations",
      "effect": "Output gap becomes more negative for longer and inflation peaks higher",
      "linking_explanation": "Backward-looking expectations cause a delayed adjustment in the economy, leading to a prolonged negative output gap and higher inflation peaks.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 7",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Increase in share of backward-looking agents",
      "effect": "Pronounced hump-shaped pattern in output and inflation",
      "linking_explanation": "As the share of backward-looking agents increases, the economy's response to shocks becomes more pronounced and prolonged, deviating from equilibrium.",
      "document_reference": "Batch 7",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    }
  ]

{
  "claims": [
    {
      "cause": "Central bank raising nominal interest rates",
      "effect": "Dampening of inflation and return to baseline of interest rates and real economy",
      "linking_explanation": "In the baseline case with fully forward-looking agents, the central bank raises nominal rates on impact, which due to benign inflation dynamics is sufficient to raise the real rate, thereby dampening inflation.",
      "document_reference": "Page 18",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Central bank raising nominal interest rates in economies with many backward-looking firms",
      "effect": "Falling real interest rate initially, adding to inflation persistence",
      "linking_explanation": "Despite the central bank raising the nominal rate sharply and persistently, the real rate actually falls initially. Since it is the real rate that determines output in this model, the falling real rate adds to inflation persistence.",
      "document_reference": "Page 18",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Increased share of backward-looking firms",
      "effect": "Lengthening of the lags of the monetary transmission mechanism",
      "linking_explanation": "As a result of the increased share of backward-looking firms, the speed at which monetary policy can affect realised inflation changes, lengthening the lags of the monetary transmission mechanism.",
      "document_reference": "Page 18",
      "quantifications": "The share of backward-looking firms in the purple economy is 80%",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "Increasing degree of backward-lookingness",
      "effect": "Shrinking share of price-setters considering supply and demand conditions, leading to persistent inflation",
      "linking_explanation": "An increasing degree of backward-lookingness implies a shrinking share of price-setters in the economy that consider supply and demand conditions when making decisions, leading to persistent inflation.",
      "document_reference": "Page 19",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    },
    {
      "cause": "High share of backward-looking agents",
      "effect": "Diminished effectiveness of monetary policy",
      "linking_explanation": "With a high share of backward-looking agents, monetary policy effectiveness - whether directly on expectations or through the output gap channel - is greatly diminished.",
      "document_reference": "Page 19",
      "quantifications": "NA",
      "modulator_uncertainty": "NA",
      "modulator_temporal": "NA"
    }
  ]

{
  "claims": [
    {
      "cause": "Monetary policy being increasingly restrictive",
      "effect": "Return the inflation rate to target",
      "linking_explanation": "When agents are increasingly backward-looking, monetary policy needs to be more restrictive to counteract inflationary pressures and guide inflation back to target.",
